sink: PILImage.open() opens and decodes any filesystem path the caller supplies, and the decoded pixels are returned to the caller as image content
why: image_path is a free-form string with no default-path restriction, no traversal check, and no allowlist of a base directory; os.path.exists(image_path) followed by PILImage.open(image_path) will open any absolute path or ../-traversed path the process can read (e.g. image_path='/home/user/other_photo.jpg' or '../../../../some/other/image.png') and return its decoded content to the MCP caller, which is an information-disclosure path-traversal / arbitrary local file read, not merely a robustness issue since it discloses file contents outside the intended ./camera directory.

why: The tool's 'name' argument flows unmodified (only spaces->underscores) from get_verified_robot_spec() -> get_verified_robot_spec_util() -> load_robot_config(), where it is joined onto the fixed specs_dir with pathlib's '/' operator and '.yaml' is appended; pathlib does not strip '..' components, so name='../../../../tmp/evil' (or any relative path ending up at a real *.yaml file outside robot_specifications/) escapes the intended directory and its YAML content is parsed and partially returned to the caller (or its parse failure/field-missing error at least confirms file existence/structure), a genuine path-traversal information-disclosure bug with no path normalization or containment check anywhere on the call path.
